basis: Neurodevelopmental disease, achalasia and alacrima define syndrome; myopathy 2/2 and contractures support musculoskeletal involvement; hyperkeratosis omitted at cap.
Amyloid deposition directly occupies tracheobronchial walls or pulmonary parenchyma; systemic organ involvement is not implied.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; developmental delay 4/8. Hearing loss 2/8 is below threshold; absent acoustic reflex alone does not establish ear damage.
Nonsyndromic hereditary sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 2/2 patients.
Autoinflammatory disease; permanent sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 40-60% across CAPS. Rash is transient; destructive CNS and skeletal disease favor severe subtypes.
Inherited degeneration of the corpus striatum causes movement and cognitive dysfunction.
Tumour originates in the sphenoid sinus, an upper-airway site. Lymphoma is only one possible histology.
Bilateral nasal alar collapse is a structural disorder of the nasal airway.
Ectopic ACTH causes hypercortisolism; direct cortisol-related proximal myopathy occurs in roughly half or more. Tumour origin varies; hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Inherited retinal degeneration directly damages photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium, causing progressive visual loss.
Renal ciliopathy/nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy are shared defining manifestations of the Senior-Loken and Bardet-Biedl phenotypes.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by hepatic, cerebral and renal disease; renal tubular dysfunction is a defining feature, retained as involved because of the primary cap.
Developmental delay 9/9 and intellectual disability 6/9 define neurologic disease. Individual cardiac defects occur in at most 2/9; overlap prevents establishing a 30% total.
Infection of axillary lymph nodes; no blood-cell, marrow or other organ disease is specified.
Rabies virus directly infects the nervous system and causes fatal encephalopathy; gastrointestinal and laryngeal findings do not establish additional direct organ damage.
Dermatophyte infection directly invades skin follicles and deeper cutaneous tissue, producing persistent granulomas and scars.
Meningioma arises from the meninges of the central nervous system.
Chronic loss of intestinal absorptive function defines disease; nutritional consequences and parenteral-feeding complications do not establish other direct organ involvement.
Umbrella concept defined by disease of the endocrine system; additional organ damage depends on the subtype.
Calculus occupies the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis; mineral composition alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Persistent neurocognitive dysfunction and muscle/joint symptoms are defining domains of Gulf War illness; symptoms in other systems do not establish direct organ damage.
Arterial and skin fragility with frequent joint laxity define the connective-tissue disorder; bowel fragility/perforation is a major criterion and HPO reports 30-79%.
Inherited terminal-complement deficiency causes immune dysfunction; meningitis and Neisserial infections are separately diagnosed infections.
Congenital segmental maldevelopment of both the spinal cord and vertebral column defines segmental spinal dysgenesis.
Persistent neutropenia with impaired innate immune defense; recurrent infections and lymphopenia occur in 30-79%. Nonimmune excludes autoimmunity; infections are separate diseases.
